requirements.requirement: Planter for kitchen windowsill - compact linear form suitable for a sill
requirements.evidence: 3 cells in a straight line: piece:-1,0,0;full + piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full with full-depth bins bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full. Overall 507mm x 384mm x 89mm (parts), low profile, fits standard windowsill depth. House rules capOpenFaces + lockJoints applied, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Sunny location - open, light-exposed growing setup
requirements.evidence: Open-top full-depth bins with soil fill, no lids/covers over plants, spaced linearly for light exposure. Plants placed in soil and visible from above (look polar 10 shows all 3 props). Suitable geometry for sunny sill use; material UV/heat resistance not verified by configurator.

Three separate bins each filled with soil and planted: basil-young in bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full (prop:1), mint-young in bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full (prop:2), parsley-young in bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full (prop:3) via fill_and_plant. All three visible in look views.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear windowsill planter (507mm long) with three full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with a different kitchen herb: basil, mint and flat-leaf parsley (young stage). Low, open-top layout maximizes sun exposure on a kitchen sill; caps and joint bolts finished, no mesh clashes or prop warnings.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
